headline: Library-scale computational mapping of activity cliffs and chemical space
label: Chemical Space Navigation Methods
summary: Ultralarge virtual libraries and growing compound collections call for scalable tools that link structural changes to bioactivity.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational navigation of large chemical spaces to connect molecular structure with bioactivity. BitBIRCH clustering is applied to large compound libraries to locate activity cliffs or delineate smooth regions of chemical space. A second study addresses ultralarge virtual libraries, which the authors frame as central to early-stage drug discovery for exploring billions of compounds. ShEPhERD-score contributes a GPU-accelerated toolkit for differentiable three-dimensional molecular similarity scoring and alignment, benchmarked on DUDE-Z virtual screening. The items differ in method and validation design, so they reflect a shared orientation rather than a uniform finding. What is new is the move toward scalable, library-level analysis, with alignment-based similarity now differentiable and GPU-accelerated.
